profile.name: Lou Correa
profile.bio: Lou Correa has represented California's 46th district since 2017 and serves on the House Judiciary Committee. He previously served in the California State Assembly, on the Orange County Board of Supervisors and in the California State Senate. Born in East Los Angeles and raised in Anaheim, he holds economics, law and business degrees.

platform.point: Believes abortion decisions belong to a woman and her doctor, and opposed overturning Roe.
Works on immigration policy through the Judiciary immigration subcommittee and the Hispanic Caucus.
Voted to block funding for vehicle kill-switch technology.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: 100% NARAL rating and opposed overturning Roe v. Wade.

security.evidence: One of four Democrats who voted to block funding for vehicle kill-switch technology.

tech.evidence: Voted against the 2022 antitrust merger filing fee bill.

profile.name: Steve Cohen
profile.bio: Steve Cohen is a San Diego broadcast journalist with about 50 years in media. He was news director at KUSI-TV for 20 years, covering California politics. He has not held elected office.

platform.point: Wants to expand housing supply and crack down on corporate price manipulation.
Pledges lower drug costs, protection for pre-existing conditions and accountability for insurers.
Commits to defending Social Security and Medicare from cuts.
Opposes earmarks and calls for transparency in federal spending.

economy.evidence: Pairs a crackdown on corporate price manipulation with opposition to earmarks and wasteful spending.

welfare.evidence: Pledges to defend Social Security and Medicare and protect pre-existing condition coverage.

profile.name: George Austin
profile.bio: George Austin is a Republican candidate for Connecticut's 2nd Congressional District from Suffield. He grew up in the construction trade, studied construction management at Central Connecticut State University and has run a contracting business in eastern Connecticut. He is the son of an immigrant from Mexico.

platform.point: Cut wasteful federal spending with a household-budget approach to taxpayer money.
Shore up Social Security and Medicare so they stay solvent for current and future retirees.
Lower taxes and regulations and widen access to homeownership for working families.
Improve VA services and the quality of care veterans receive.
Set guardrails on AI so its gains reach American workers rather than only large tech firms.
Protect the unborn and defend Second Amendment rights.

economy.evidence: Campaign calls for lower taxes, fewer regulations and cuts to government waste.

liberty.evidence: Averages opposition to abortion (community norms) with defense of Second Amendment gun rights (individual choice).

tech.evidence: Calls for AI guardrails so innovation benefits workers and not just tech monopolies.

profile.notes: Little detail is published on his specific legislative proposals; liberty score rests on convention coverage of his abortion and gun stances.

profile.name: Joseph Arminio
profile.bio: Joseph Arminio is a Wilmington native with a Ph.D. in political science from MIT and a bachelor's degree from Johns Hopkins. He chaired the National Coalition for Defense, taught at American University and Lincoln University, published a Maryland newspaper and has written several books on American policy and history. He ran in Maryland's 2008 Republican congressional primary.

platform.point: Adopt his American Prosperity Plan to address stagflation and high public and private debt.
End open-ended wars, avoid entanglement in Ukraine and Iran, and push Israel toward a two-state solution.
Require formal debate in high school and teach economic history from primary sources.
Uphold the Second Amendment and the full Constitution.
Enforce existing immigration law and end sanctuary cities.

liberty.evidence: Campaign pledges to uphold Second Amendment gun rights; other liberty issues not addressed.

immigration.evidence: Calls for enforcing immigration law and ending sanctuary cities.

foreign.evidence: Opposes endless wars and entanglements in Ukraine and Iran.

profile.notes: Wikipedia's race page lists him as a medical doctor, but his campaign biography describes a political science Ph.D.; the campaign description is used here.
